topic_ko: 사하라 이남 아프리카의 영어, 특히 현지 언어의 영향으로 Howzit!·robots·lekker·"just now" 같은 독특한 표현을 지닌 남아프리카 영어

passage: The term African English could mean English used anywhere in Africa, but it usually refers to the English of Sub-Saharan Africa.
Today, English is an official language in 27 countries on the continent.
One major variety is South African English, which has been official in South Africa ever since the British arrived in 1795.
The many languages spoken in the country have strongly shaped the English used there.
As a result, South African English has some colorful words and phrases.
People may greet each other by saying Howzit! instead of asking how things are going, traffic lights are known as robots, and lekker means "nice."
Visitors are often puzzled when a South African promises, "I'll do it just now."
The phrase does not promise immediate action; it only means the task might be done at some point later.
choices: the features of African English, especially South African English
the history of British colonies in Asia
why traffic rules differ around the world
the number of languages spoken in Africa
how to make friends in South Africa
theme.explanation_ko: 사하라 이남 아프리카의 영어, 그중 현지 언어의 영향으로 독특한 표현을 지닌 남아프리카 영어를 다루므로 ①가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ② 아시아가 아니라 아프리카를 다룬다. ③ 신호등은 robots 라는 단어 예시일 뿐이다. ④ 언어의 개수는 제시되지 않는다. ⑤ 인사말 Howzit! 은 표현의 예일 뿐 친구 사귀는 법이 아니다.

order.given: For one, South African English has some colorful words and phrases.

blocks.A: English speakers from other countries are sometimes confused when a South African says, "I'll do it just now." That does not mean that they will do it now. It actually means they might do it sometime in the future.
blocks.B: Traffic lights in South Africa are called robots, and lekker means "nice."
blocks.C: For instance, when they meet someone, they might say Howzit! instead of "Hello, how's it going?"

order.explanation_ko: 다채로운 표현이 있다는 주어진 문장 뒤에 (C) For instance 로 첫 예(Howzit!), (B) 단어 예(robots, lekker), (A) 외국인을 헷갈리게 하는 "just now"와 그 실제 뜻 순서로 이어지므로 ①이다.
order.distractor_ko: (C)의 For instance 는 주어진 문장 바로 뒤에서 예시를 열어야 하고, (A)는 오해와 그 정정까지 담은 마무리라 맨 끝에 와야 한다.

passage_marked.text: For one, South African English has some colorful words and phrases.
For instance, when they meet someone, they might say Howzit! instead of "Hello, how's it going?"
Traffic lights in South Africa are called robots, and lekker means "nice."
English speakers from other countries are sometimes confused when a South African says, "I'll do it just now."
It actually means they might do it sometime in the future.

insert.distractor_ko: ①②③ 자리에는 That 이 가리킬 "just now"가 아직 나오지 않았고, ⑤ 자리는 actually 로 정정한 뒤라 부정이 너무 늦게 나온다.
